newsitem.title: JAPAN: Euro carmakers seek cut in Japan's car tax.
newsitem.headline: Euro carmakers seek cut in Japan's car tax.

text.p: European carmakers called on the Japanese government on Tuesday to abolish Japan's automobile acquisition tax when it raises its consumption tax to five percent from three percent next April.

The European Automobile Manufacturers' Association (ACEA) said in a statement that the director-general of its Tokyo office, Anthony Millington, told a meeting on Tuesday that the increase in the consumption tax would reduce sales of imported vehicles by three to four percent.
He said also it could revive trade friction with the United States and the European Union.
Japanese consumers now pay an acquisition tax of five percent as well as the three percent consumption tax when they buy cars.
